northStar.name: AXIS Performance OS
northStar.productContract: Turn protocols into executable activity, preserve what actually happened, attach evidence to factual encounters, and support evidence-bounded adaptation without allowing AI to become the truth owner.

stages.goal: Establish a trustworthy baseline, converge product truth, remove documentation drift, and prevent new work from building on an unresolved release state.
exit: current merged runtime status is factually recorded
production certification failures are understood or explicitly held
product north star and capability manifest are repository-authoritative
long-range stages and boundaries are recorded
no new feature work bypasses the program contracts

stages.goal: Move from version-shaped source history toward capability-shaped ownership and tests without rewriting the product.
exit: critical capabilities have current owners
version-specific compatibility layers have a retirement map
tests are increasingly capability-oriented
release truth has one clear repository path

stages.goal: Make visible state, interaction geometry, typography, motion, localization and accessibility deterministic product contracts rather than incidental CSS behavior.
exit: semantic components exist for primary action, secondary state, metrics, evidence and review surfaces
critical state transitions have geometry tolerances
empty or hidden states create zero unintended geometry
reduced motion and mobile WebKit remain first-class

stages.goal: Extract deterministic domain decisions from DOM, browser storage and deployment-specific code using strangler migration.
exit: events-reducer-state-projection decisions can run without a browser
current browser owners remain compatible during migration
runtime fixtures cover continuation and remaining-route decisions

stages.goal: Create append-only factual lineage for execution and evidence while retaining compatibility snapshots until replay is proven.
exit: new runtime actions have stable event identities
encounters can be reconstructed deterministically
evidence source and provenance are explicit
migration does not invalidate existing history

stages.goal: Evolve Flow into a protocol runtime that can express intended execution, constraints, bounded substitutions and completion rules.
exit: protocol intent remains separate from performed reality
runtime can adapt route to explicit constraints
temporary overrides carry provenance
protocol definitions are portable and testable

stages.goal: Unify encounter chronology, evidence, observations and outcomes into a trustworthy longitudinal performance graph.
exit: evidence never impersonates another encounter
observed and inferred data remain distinct
evolution views derive from factual lineage
no opaque progress score becomes truth

stages.goal: Productize identity and durable local-first synchronization without making the network the live workout owner.
exit: account is optional for core execution
sync is idempotent and conflict-bounded
export and deletion lifecycle are explicit
platform adapters share domain contracts

stages.goal: Add a separate organization workspace for coaches and performance organizations without polluting the participant execution shell.
exit: organization and tenancy model exists
roles and permissions are explicit
protocol assignment and review workflows exist
audit events are durable
participant app remains quiet and execution-first

stages.goal: Add AI recommendations as auditable proposals over factual state, never as silent truth writers.
exit: observed inferred recommended and decided layers are separate
recommendations record input fingerprint model reason confidence and decision
human acceptance is required for authoritative protocol changes
AI failure preserves a usable deterministic path

stages.goal: Turn Object, Protocol, Runtime, Encounter and Evidence contracts into a documented integration surface that third parties can execute and extend.
exit: stable schemas are versioned independently from UI releases
reference SDK can define and execute protocol objects
integration tests prove deterministic behavior
open-source boundaries do not expose secrets or enterprise-only data

stages.goal: Validate real organizational value before broad scaling, then harden security, integrations and operations from observed needs.
exit: real pilot organizations complete protocol-to-review workflows
time saved data completeness and execution variance can be measured
security and retention controls match deployment needs
integration priorities are driven by pilot evidence rather than feature speculation
